Senior faculty members with active research grants may access journals and archives classified as peer-reviewed and restricted.
Graduate students enrolled in doctoral programs can download theses marked confidential and unpublished manuscripts.
Librarians assigned to digital collections are allowed to modify archived catalogs and indexes labeled institution-wide.
Research assistants with verified campus accounts may read academic and licensed datasets and journals.
Visiting scholars holding temporary affiliations can view historical manuscripts and encrypted repositories.
Journals and archives classified as peer-reviewed and restricted are accessible to senior faculty members who hold active research grants.
Graduate students enrolled in doctoral programs may download theses and manuscripts marked as confidential or unpublished.
Catalogues and indexes labelled as archived or institution-wide may be modified by librarians who are assigned to digital collections.
Research assistants with verified campus accounts are permitted to read datasets and journals designated as academic and licensed.
Manuscripts and repositories categorised as historical and encrypted are available for viewing by visiting scholars with temporary affiliations.
Researchers with expired library cards or incomplete identity verification cannot modify catalogs and indexes labeled confidential and institutional.
Staff members holding inactive accounts or revoked privileges may not read licensed archives and protected datasets.
Cardiologists with emergency clearance or active surgical duties may access records and scans marked urgent or confidential.
Appointments and profiles designated internal or protected can be viewed by receptionists with front-desk authorization or weekend assignments.

Therapists who are accredited or counselors who are assigned to rehabilitation and employed full-time may read assessments and notes that are confidential and encrypted when the assessments or notes are associated with ongoing therapy and the access request is submitted during approved consultation hours.

Consultants or vendors who are unaffiliated, remotely connected, or lacking security clearance may not read assessments and notes that are encrypted and confidential when the assessments or notes are related to intensive care and the connection is established through a public network.

Faculty members may download manuscripts that are archived and  multilingual and restricted catalogs only if they are requested during library opening hours and the user is connected through the university VPN.

Temporary staff cannot download access theses and datasets that are encrypted, institution-owned, and unpublished when the theses or datasets are awaiting faculty approval or the user is connected through a public network.
Doctors and nurses may read and modify records and schedules when the records relate to patients currently under their care or the schedules concern clinic sessions taking place that day.

text: Pharmacists and physicians can access and update prescriptions and inventories when the prescriptions are associated with active treatments or the inventories correspond to medications awaiting dispensing.

Receptionists and care coordinators may view and edit appointments and referrals only if the appointments are scheduled within the current operating period or the referrals are pending specialist review.

Condition.resources.Cond.res.name: appointments
Cond.res.props: scheduled within the current operating period

text: Laboratory technicians and pathologists are allowed to read and revise reports and requests provided that the reports pertain to tests completed during the current case or the requests originate from ongoing patient assessments.

Condition.resources.Cond.res.name: reports
Cond.res.props: pertain to tests completed during the current case

text: Radiologists and imaging specialists may access and modify scans and reports when the scans are linked to patients undergoing active diagnosis or the reports are awaiting clinical confirmation.
Visiting researchers and external consultants may not download or modify manuscripts and datasets if the manuscripts are under embargo or the datasets are restricted to active research programs.
Student assistants and temporary staff are allowed to access or delete archives and publications unless the archives contain unreleased findings or the publications are awaiting editorial approval.
Guest scholars and contract analysts cannot read or update catalogs and records if the catalogs include confidential collections or the records relate to ongoing investigations.

Interns and volunteer researchers may not access or alter journals and repositories when the journals are reserved for peer-review activities or the repositories contain material subject to licensing restrictions.

Condition.resources.Cond.res.name: repositories
Cond.res.props: contain material subject to licensing restrictions

text: External auditors and visiting fellows are not allowed to download or edit theses and documents if the theses are pending formal publication or the documents belong to restricted research initiatives.

Senior researchers and accredited librarians may access restricted manuscripts and curated datasets when the researchers are assigned to an active research project and the manuscripts belong to the project collection and the request originates from the institute network.

Condition.subjects.Cond.subj.name: researchers
Cond.subj.props: assigned to an active research project

text: Certified archivists and permanent fellows may read historical journals and classified repositories when the fellows are participating in an approved study and the repositories support that study and the connection is established through the secure library network.

Condition.envNetworks: connection is established through the secure library network

text: Lead scientists and authorized cataloguers may access peer-reviewed publications and indexed records when the scientists hold responsibility for the current research program and the publications are associated with that program and the session is conducted from an internal network segment.

Condition.subjects.Cond.subj.name: scientists
Cond.subj.props: responsible for the current research program

Condition.envNetworks: session is conducted from an internal network segment

text: Principal investigators and senior specialist staff may view and upload draft theses and annotated documents when the investigators are engaged in an ongoing institute initiative and the documents are part of that initiative and the access request comes through the protected campus network.

Condition.subjects.Cond.subj.name: investigators
Cond.subj.props: engaged in an ongoing institute initiative

Condition.envNetworks: access request comes through the protected campus network

text: Junior researchers and digital curators may read archived reports and validated collections unless the researchers are working on an expired project and the collections are related to that project and the network connection uses the institute's secure infrastructure.

Temporary nurses and contract technicians may not access confidential records and encrypted backups if the nurses are assigned to departments outside the patient's care unit or the records belong to a restricted treatment program or the request originates from an unsecured network.

Condition.subjects.Cond.subj.name: nurses
Cond.subj.props: assigned to departments outside the patient's care unit

Condition.resources.Cond.res.name: records
Cond.res.props: belong to a restricted treatment program

text: Trainee physicians and visiting specialists are allowed to view sensitive logs and protected databases unless the specialists are participating in observational duties only or the databases contain information from high-security clinical systems or the connection is established through a public network.

Condition.resources.Cond.res.name: databases
Cond.res.props: contain information from high-security clinical systems

Condition.envNetworks: connection is established through a public network

text: Probationary administrators and external support engineers cannot access critical servers or restricted archives when the administrators have not completed mandatory authorization training or the archives store regulated patient information and the operation take place during weekends.

Condition.envDatetimes: the operation take place during weekends

text: Agency staff and temporary analyst staff may not read classified reports and secured repositories when the analysts are assigned to short-term operational tasks and the reports relate to restricted medical investigations and the access takes place outside working-hours.

Junior operators and contract auditors are not allowed to access protected datasets and confidential records when the operators are working under limited-access assignments and the datasets are associated with sensitive patient programs and the request is made through the weekend or outside working-hours.

Undergraduate students who are enrolled in distance-learning programs and hold temporary library memberships and have overdue account restrictions may not access journals when the students are first-year enrollees and visiting scholars and the journals are reserved for faculty research.

Research assistants who work part-time and belong to external partner institutions and have limited borrowing privileges are not allowed to read archives when the assistants are assigned to short-term projects and guest researchers and the archives are designated for confidential studies.

Visiting students who are registered for audit courses and possess temporary credentials and have not completed library orientation cannot access repositories unless the students are participating in exchange programs and contract researchers and the repositories contain restricted academic materials.

External collaborators who are affiliated with partner organizations and use provisional accounts and have limited authorization may not access theses unless the collaborators are involved in pilot initiatives and adjunct researchers and the theses are under publication embargo.

Student volunteers who assist library operations and hold temporary access badges are not allowed to access manuscripts only if the volunteers are assigned to non-research duties or visiting academic projects and the manuscripts belong to special collections.

Senior physicians who are assigned to critical care units and have completed data-governance training, and senior nurses who are assigned to inpatient services and hold advanced care certifications, may read or write clinical records provided that the physicians are currently responsible for the patient's treatment or the nurses are participating in the patient's care team or the records support an advanced episode of care.

text: Clinical researchers who are employed by the medical center and possess approved study credentials and have completed compliance certification, and data analysts who are assigned to research operations and hold authorized system accounts and have completed security training, may read and update datasets provided that the researchers are working on an approved study and the analysts are assigned to that study and the datasets belong to the approved research project.

Health information managers assigned to records administration who possess active professional accreditation and have completed annual audits, and senior compliance officers who are employed in regulatory oversight, may browse through archives if the managers are responsible for record maintenance and the officers are conducting an authorized review and the archives are older than one year.

Laboratory supervisors who are assigned to diagnostic services or hold active supervisory roles, and pathology specialists who are employed in clinical laboratories and possess superior professional qualifications and have completed a security course, may delete reports when the supervisors are overseeing the testing workflow and the specialists are validating diagnostic findings and the reports are associated with active laboratory cases.

Senior system administrators who are assigned to healthcare infrastructure, and database engineers who are employed in data management services  and have completed compliance training, may modify critical databases provided that the administrators have been employed for more than 10 years and operations are performed during weekends.

Faculty researchers with active appointments may read and download journals and theses that are peer-reviewed or faculty-curated or citation-indexed when the journals' publisher is ACM and the theses belong to departmental collections.

Graduate students aged less than 30 may access and download papers and datasets that are course-related or supervisor-approved or department-licensed when the papers are required for seminars and the datasets support active research projects.

Library staff with smart accounts may read and archive manuscripts and proceedings that are catalogued or preservation-ready or faculty-submitted only if the manuscripts are assigned to the physics collection or the proceedings relate to mathematics conferences.

Doctoral candidates with research clearance may view and download preprints and datasets that are advisor-endorsed or grant-funded or repository-approved provided that the preprints concern active dissertation work and the datasets are linked to approved research groups.

Professors with teaching assignments may access and share textbooks and online material that are department-approved or access-restricted only if the textbooks are used in approved courses and the online material support supervised tutorials and the operations occur via the VPN or the internal network.

Condition.envNetworks: operations occur via the internal network

text: Contractors with limited authorization may not access or modify databases that are privacy-sensitive when the DB records belong to active treatments or access occur from an external network or during weekends.

Condition.envNetworks: access occur from an external network

text: Visiting interns with limited access are not allowed to read or delete reports that are restricted-access and archives that are audit-protected or security-classified when the reports contain ongoing investigation findings and the archives store private healthcare information.
External consultants with non-clinical roles cannot access or update logs and documents that are privacy-protected  when the logs document active security events, or during weekends and holidays.

Temporary volunteer assistants cannot view or modify confidential datasets and legally protected or patient-linked records unless the datasets are older than 5 years and the records are older than 10 years.

Third-party technicians are not allowed to access or delete encrypted backups or compliance-monitored and security-sensitive records, unless the backups support live recovery operations or the records are older than 5 years.
